title: Operational Mapping: SLI → Objective Mapping + Adaptive Rollout Playbook
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Create a reproducible SLI-to-OKR mapping matrix and an operational rollout playbook that ties: 1) SLIs and their weight toward reliability objectives, 2) automated error-budget burn detection, and 3) an adaptive escalation + rollout policy enforced via Console. This ticket produces: a canonical mapping table, a set of Grafana/Console dashboards, an automated runbook flow for three escalation tiers (notify, mitigate, rollback), and rollout guardrails for canary/graded deploys that throttle feature rollouts based on active error-budget burn. The goal is to reduce reactive firefighting and give product/engineering leads clear, quantitative gates for pausing rollouts or enabling mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI → OKR mapping completed for top 8 reliability objectives and published to Confluence
Grafana and Console dashboards show per-initiative error-budget burn and projected runway with 1h and 24h forecasts
Runbook automation: burn-rate > 2x for 60m triggers Tier 1 notify; burn-rate > 5x for 30m triggers Tier 2 mitigate; sustained Tier 2 for 90m triggers Tier 3 rollback policy executed
Console rollout policy integrated: canary weight automatically capped or rolled back when Tier 2/3 conditions are met
Stakeholder sign-off from Platform, Observability, and Product on thresholds and communication flow
success_metrics: 30% reduction in cross-team P1 incidents attributed to rollout regressions within 3 months
50% fewer emergency rollback actions executed manually (automation covers majority)
>80% of active initiatives adopting the mapping matrix within one quarter
Error-budget alert noise reduced (false positives) by 25% after tuning
risks: Overly aggressive thresholds causing unnecessary rollbacks and blocking releases
Telemetry gaps (missing latency percentiles or request-type breakdowns) leading to incorrect burn calculations
Teams bypassing policy if policy is perceived as blocking velocity (change management needed)
Dependence on Console features and on-call routing (ENG work could delay rollout)
rollout_plan: Discovery (1 week): inventory active initiatives, collect current SLIs and dashboards
Design (1.5 weeks): propose SLI weights, draft runbook tiers, draft Console rollout guardrail config
Implement (2 sprints): dashboard panels, runbook automation playbooks, Console policy hooks (canary throttles)
Canary (2 weeks): enable policy for 2 low-risk initiatives and observe behavior under synthetic and real traffic
Org rollout (3 weeks): onboarding sessions, template provisioning, and adoption incentives
Post-rollout tuning (ongoing): weekly adjustments to thresholds and playbook steps for first 6 weeks
decisions: Primary SLIs to be used for initial mapping: p95 latency for Gen endpoint, availability (5xx rate) for serving, and median queueing time for burst-prone routes
Use burn-rate heuristic (error budget consumed per unit time relative to baseline) instead of absolute budget thresholds to support variable traffic patterns
Three-tier operational model (notify / mitigate / rollback) chosen to balance automation and human-in-the-loop escalation
Consolidate alerts into a single Console policy per initiative to avoid duplicated PagerDuty noise
